label: late-episode D2 dip after a1 / S1-belief; D1 dip after a1->S2
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 2) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * np.clip(belief_lo,-4,4) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * np.clip(belief_lo,-4,4) * ep_trial
explanation: Raw reset gate r43 sits near 1 (mean 0.989) and dips mostly at D2 and late in the episode; timing alone gives R^2 0.53. Beyond timing, every effect grows roughly linearly with episode trial (scaling terms by ep_trial beat unscaled terms, 0.49 vs 0.42 dev, and also beat exponential or hinge scalings). At D2 the gate is lower after choosing a1 and higher after a2 (largest weight), lowest for a1 -> S1 common, and lower the more the ideal observer believes S1 is good (belief_lo, clipped). At GO there is a small dip with S1 belief. At D1 it dips after a previous a1 -> S2 rare trial; the previous-reward term gets about zero weight. In short, the gate closes late in the episode when the agent is on the a1/S1 side. The 7 observed-only terms (no future, hidden or model-output variables) score test R^2 beyond timing 0.561 (dev 0.563), about 97% of the all-cue ceiling of 0.58 and level with all observed (0.56). Belief deciles alone (0.35) do about as well as policy deciles (0.36), so dropping the model value/policy costs little. The remaining misses are late-episode windows where the D2 dips are deeper than the linear time scaling predicts.

issues: The test score reproduces: 0.561 beyond timing, against an all-cue ceiling of 0.58. Scaling by ep_trial also beats the unscaled terms (0.471 test), as claimed.

The claim that ep_trial scaling beats exponential scalings is false. Swapping ep_trial for np.exp(ep_trial/30) in the same 7 terms gives 0.586 test, against 0.561 for linear. The late-episode growth is convex, and that matches the 'misses' note that late D2 dips run deeper than the linear fit predicts.

One of the 7 terms does nothing. (phase==D1)*(prev_reward==1)*ep_trial gets weight about -4e-7, and dropping it leaves test R^2 at 0.561. The GO belief term is also small: dropping it costs only 0.007.

The D1 dip is partly misdescribed. The residual table shows D1 after a1 S2 r at -0.016 and after a1 S2 u at -0.008, so a reward obtained in S2 deepens the dip. The worst-fit examples include D1 values of 0.82-0.85 after rewarded S2 trials, including a2->S2 common ones. A D1 prev_state==2 x prev_reward==1 term adds +0.006 test, so the reward does matter there once it is conditioned on S2. It is not simply 'about zero'.

Systematic errors remain at D2, depending on the previous trial. The terms underpredict D2 after a1 S2 r by +0.008 and overpredict it after a1 S1 u by -0.009. These are about the same size as the main D2 effects (about ±0.012). Adding a D2 prev_action==1 term helps (+0.014), but the a1 S2 r gap persists at +0.011 even with the improved terms. The model's D2 gate tracks the previous choice more than the ideal-observer belief does.
